chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the characteristic infrared absorption signature of an aliphatic alcohol (e.g., 1-butanol)?

options.label: A
options.text: A strong, broad absorption band at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ resulting from hydrogen-bonded O-H stretching vibrations.

options.label: B
options.text: A sharp, intense peak at 1715 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: Absence of any peaks above 3000 cm⁻¹.

options.label: D
options.text: A sharp, narrow peak at 2250 cm⁻¹.

questions.correct_answer: A strong, broad absorption band at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ resulting from hydrogen-bonded O-H stretching vibrations.
questions.explanation: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding broadens and intensifies the hydroxyl O-H stretch at ~3300 cm⁻¹.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: At what diagnostic wavenumber do aliphatic ketones (e.g., 2-pentanone) exhibit an intense IR absorption peak?

options.label: A
options.text: At 3300 cm⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.text: At 1600 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: At approximately 1715 cm⁻¹ (strong, sharp C=O stretching vibration).

options.label: D
options.text: At 2150 cm⁻¹.

questions.correct_answer: At approximately 1715 cm⁻¹ (strong, sharp C=O stretching vibration).
questions.explanation: The large dipole moment change of the carbonyl group produces a sharp, intense peak at ~1715 cm⁻¹.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What two distinct infrared absorption features unambiguously identify an aldehyde functional group?

options.label: A
options.text: A sharp C=O stretch at ~1725 cm⁻¹ and a characteristic Fermi doublet of C-H stretches at 2720 and 2820 cm⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.text: Only a single peak at 1650 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: A single triple-bond peak at 2200 cm⁻¹.

options.label: D
options.text: A broad O-H stretch at 3300 cm⁻¹ and an ester C-O at 1200 cm⁻¹.

questions.correct_answer: A sharp C=O stretch at ~1725 cm⁻¹ and a characteristic Fermi doublet of C-H stretches at 2720 and 2820 cm⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Aldehydes exhibit a carbonyl peak at ~1725 cm⁻¹ plus two weak-to-medium C-H stretching bands at 2720 and 2820 cm⁻¹.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What two diagnostic infrared absorption peaks confirm the presence of a terminal alkyne (e.g., 1-hexyne)?

options.label: A
options.text: A sharp sp C-H stretch at 3300 cm⁻¹ and a weak-to-medium C≡C triple bond stretch at ~2120 cm⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.text: A broad band at 1600 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: A broad O-H band at 3400 cm⁻¹ and a C=O peak at 1715 cm⁻¹.

options.label: D
options.text: A nitrile peak at 2250 cm⁻¹ only.

questions.correct_answer: A sharp sp C-H stretch at 3300 cm⁻¹ and a weak-to-medium C≡C triple bond stretch at ~2120 cm⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Terminal alkynes display a sharp sp C-H stretch at 3300 cm⁻¹ and a C≡C stretch at 2100–2200 cm⁻¹.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What infrared spectral pattern is diagnostic for a carboxylic acid functional group?

options.label: A
options.text: Only C-H stretching at 2950 cm⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.text: A single peak at 2250 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: An extremely broad O-H stretching envelope spanning 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ overlapping sp³ C-H bonds, combined with a sharp C=O peak at ~1710 cm⁻¹.

options.label: D
options.text: A sharp O-H peak at 3600 cm⁻¹ with no carbonyl peak.

questions.correct_answer: An extremely broad O-H stretching envelope spanning 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ overlapping sp³ C-H bonds, combined with a sharp C=O peak at ~1710 cm⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen-bonded carboxylic acid dimers produce an extremely broad O-H band overlapping C-H peaks from 2500 to 3300 cm⁻¹.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why do primary aliphatic amines (R-NH₂) display two distinct peaks in the 3300–3500 cm⁻¹ region of their IR spectrum?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the amine is contaminated with water.

options.label: B
options.text: Due to two independent vibrational modes: symmetrical and asymmetrical N-H stretching of the NH₂ group.

options.label: C
options.text: Because one peak corresponds to C-N stretching.

options.label: D
options.text: Because primary amines exist as an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers.

questions.correct_answer: Due to two independent vibrational modes: symmetrical and asymmetrical N-H stretching of the NH₂ group.
questions.explanation: The NH₂ group undergoes both symmetric and asymmetric stretching, producing a characteristic two-pronged doublet.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Conjugation Effect on IR Carbonyl Frequency
questions.question: How does conjugation with an adjacent C=C double bond or aromatic ring affect the carbonyl IR stretching frequency?

options.label: A
options.text: It lowers (red-shifts) the stretching frequency by 20–40 cm⁻¹ (e.g., from 1715 cm⁻¹ down to 1685 cm⁻¹) due to increased single-bond character.

options.label: B
options.text: It has zero effect on the frequency.

options.label: C
options.text: It splits the carbonyl peak into four peaks.

options.label: D
options.text: It raises the frequency by 100 cm⁻¹.

questions.correct_answer: It lowers (red-shifts) the stretching frequency by 20–40 cm⁻¹ (e.g., from 1715 cm⁻¹ down to 1685 cm⁻¹) due to increased single-bond character.
questions.explanation: Resonance delocalization gives the carbonyl bond more single-bond character, lowering the force constant k and decreasing wavenumber.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Ester vs Ketone IR Carbonyl Frequency
questions.question: Why does an aliphatic ester (R-COOR') absorb at a higher frequency (~1735–1745 cm⁻¹) than an aliphatic ketone (~1715 cm⁻¹)?

options.label: A
options.text: Esters are conjugated with double bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: Ketones contain nitrogen atoms.

options.label: C
options.text: Esters have lower molecular weights than ketones.

options.label: D
options.text: The electronegative ester oxygen pulls electron density inductively through σ bonds, strengthening the C=O double bond and increasing its force constant.

questions.correct_answer: The electronegative ester oxygen pulls electron density inductively through σ bonds, strengthening the C=O double bond and increasing its force constant.
questions.explanation: Strong inductive electron withdrawal by the alkoxy oxygen shortens and strengthens the carbonyl bond, shifting absorption to ~1735 cm⁻¹.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Nitrile C≡N vs Alkyne C≡C IR Frequency
questions.question: How can an infrared spectrum distinguish between a nitrile (R-C≡N) and an internal alkyne (R-C≡C-R)?

options.label: A
options.text: Nitriles absorb at 1715 cm⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.text: A nitrile exhibits a strong, sharp peak at 2250 cm⁻¹ (due to its large dipole moment), whereas an internal alkyne is very weak or IR inactive (zero dipole change).

options.label: C
options.text: Nitriles are completely invisible in IR.

options.label: D
options.text: Alkynes absorb at 3300 cm⁻¹ exclusively.

questions.correct_answer: A nitrile exhibits a strong, sharp peak at 2250 cm⁻¹ (due to its large dipole moment), whereas an internal alkyne is very weak or IR inactive (zero dipole change).
questions.explanation: The polarized C≡N bond creates a strong dipole change giving an intense peak at 2250 cm⁻¹; nonpolar alkynes give weak/absent peaks.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the diagnostic role of the 'fingerprint region' (400–1400 cm⁻¹) in infrared spectroscopy?

options.label: A
options.text: It determines the optical rotation of enantiomers.

options.label: B
options.text: It identifies whether an alcohol is primary or tertiary directly.

options.label: C
options.text: It contains complex, unique bending and skeletal vibrational patterns that serve as an unambiguous 'fingerprint' to confirm the exact identity of a molecule against a database.

options.label: D
options.text: It measures the molecular weight of the compound.

questions.correct_answer: It contains complex, unique bending and skeletal vibrational patterns that serve as an unambiguous 'fingerprint' to confirm the exact identity of a molecule against a database.
questions.explanation: The fingerprint region represents coupled whole-molecule vibrations unique to each individual compound.

options.text: The electronegative ester oxygen pulls electron density inductively through σ bonds, strengthening the C=O double bond and increasing its force constant.

options.label: B
options.text: Esters have lower molecular weights than ketones.

options.label: C
options.text: Ketones contain nitrogen atoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Esters are conjugated with double bonds.

questions.correct_answer: The electronegative ester oxygen pulls electron density inductively through σ bonds, strengthening the C=O double bond and increasing its force constant.
questions.explanation: Strong inductive electron withdrawal by the alkoxy oxygen shortens and strengthens the carbonyl bond, shifting absorption to ~1735 cm⁻¹.

questions.topic: Nitrile C≡N vs Alkyne C≡C IR Frequency
questions.question: How can an infrared spectrum distinguish between a nitrile (R-C≡N) and an internal alkyne (R-C≡C-R)?

options.label: A
options.text: A nitrile exhibits a strong, sharp peak at 2250 cm⁻¹ (due to its large dipole moment), whereas an internal alkyne is very weak or IR inactive (zero dipole change).

options.label: B
options.text: Nitriles absorb at 1715 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: Nitriles are completely invisible in IR.

options.label: D
options.text: Alkynes absorb at 3300 cm⁻¹ exclusively.

questions.correct_answer: A nitrile exhibits a strong, sharp peak at 2250 cm⁻¹ (due to its large dipole moment), whereas an internal alkyne is very weak or IR inactive (zero dipole change).
questions.explanation: The polarized C≡N bond creates a strong dipole change giving an intense peak at 2250 cm⁻¹; nonpolar alkynes give weak/absent peaks.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the diagnostic role of the 'fingerprint region' (400–1400 cm⁻¹) in infrared spectroscopy?

options.label: A
options.text: It measures the molecular weight of the compound.

options.label: B
options.text: It identifies whether an alcohol is primary or tertiary directly.

options.label: C
options.text: It contains complex, unique bending and skeletal vibrational patterns that serve as an unambiguous 'fingerprint' to confirm the exact identity of a molecule against a database.

options.label: D
options.text: It determines the optical rotation of enantiomers.

questions.correct_answer: It contains complex, unique bending and skeletal vibrational patterns that serve as an unambiguous 'fingerprint' to confirm the exact identity of a molecule against a database.
questions.explanation: The fingerprint region represents coupled whole-molecule vibrations unique to each individual compound.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What two distinct infrared absorption features unambiguously identify an aldehyde functional group?

questions.explanation: Aldehydes exhibit a carbonyl peak at ~1725 cm⁻¹ plus two weak-to-medium C-H stretching bands at 2720 and 2820 cm⁻¹.

questions.question: What two diagnostic infrared absorption peaks confirm the presence of a terminal alkyne (e.g., 1-hexyne)?

options.text: A sharp sp C-H stretch at 3300 cm⁻¹ and a weak-to-medium C≡C triple bond stretch at ~2120 cm⁻¹.

questions.question: What infrared spectral pattern is diagnostic for a carboxylic acid functional group?

options.label: B
options.text: A single peak at 2250 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: Only C-H stretching at 2950 cm⁻¹.

options.label: D
options.text: An extremely broad O-H stretching envelope spanning 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ overlapping sp³ C-H bonds, combined with a sharp C=O peak at ~1710 cm⁻¹.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why do primary aliphatic amines (R-NH₂) display two distinct peaks in the 3300–3500 cm⁻¹ region of their IR spectrum?

options.label: A
options.text: Because one peak corresponds to C-N stretching.

options.label: B
options.text: Because the amine is contaminated with water.

options.label: C
options.text: Because primary amines exist as an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers.

options.label: D
options.text: Due to two independent vibrational modes: symmetrical and asymmetrical N-H stretching of the NH₂ group.

questions.correct_answer: Due to two independent vibrational modes: symmetrical and asymmetrical N-H stretching of the NH₂ group.
questions.explanation: The NH₂ group undergoes both symmetric and asymmetric stretching, producing a characteristic two-pronged doublet.
